## Design and boundaries

This analysis predicts `major_donor_next_fy` for constituents whose current
annual giving is below $2,000, including zero. A positive outcome is $2,000–$15,000
in the following July–June fiscal year. FY2021–FY2024 are development only:
train on FY2021 and validate FY2022, then expand training through FY2022 and
FY2023 to validate FY2023 and FY2024. Each validation outcome is observed in
the following year. FY2025 features with FY2026 outcomes are reserved for final
group testing; FY2026 is an unlabeled prediction cohort. Neither enters this
analysis's model selection, preprocessing, or evaluation. The group should
freeze its choices before using the final test; FY2026 needs FY2027 outcomes.

Within each fold, compare identical models and observations with and without
solicitation-response variables. Campaign response is a **proxy**: the source
records a same-constituent, same-code payment in the fiscal year, not proven
causation. Campaign start dates are year markers, not contact dates. Current
and trailing features are available by year end. Snapshot attributes,
cultivation assignment, IDs, split markers, and all future outcomes are excluded.

```{r setup}
#| include: false
if (dir.exists(".r-lib")) .libPaths(c(normalizePath(".r-lib"), .libPaths()))
required <- c("caret", "pROC", "randomForest", "glmnet", "xgboost", "dplyr",
              "tidyr", "ggplot2", "readr", "foreach", "doParallel")
missing_packages <- required[!vapply(required, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_packages)) stop("Install required R packages: ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "))
library(caret)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(foreach)
library(doParallel)
set.seed(42)
```

```{r data}
analytic <- read_csv("Data_Files/constituent_fiscal_year_analytic.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(analytic[c("constituent_id", "fiscal_year")]))
stopifnot(all(is.na(analytic$major_donor_next_fy[analytic$fiscal_year == 2026])))
stopifnot(all(analytic$data_split[analytic$fiscal_year == 2025] == "final_test"))
stopifnot(all(analytic$data_split[analytic$fiscal_year == 2026] == "prediction"))
# Retain only development data before any feature selection or summaries.
dev <- analytic %>% filter(fiscal_year %in% 2021:2024, annual_giving < 2000,
                           !is.na(major_donor_next_fy))
rm(analytic)
# Use numeric donor characteristics only, with a strict outcome/identifier audit.
excluded <- grepl("^next_fy_|_snapshot$|^cultivation_", names(dev)) |
  names(dev) %in% c("constituent_id", "fiscal_year", "data_split", "major_donor_next_fy")
candidates <- names(dev)[!excluded & vapply(dev, is.numeric, logical(1))]
solicitation <- candidates[grepl("^(solicitations|responses|campaign_|unique_campaigns_solicited|prior_fy_solicitations|prior_fy_campaign_responses|trailing_3_fy_solicitations|trailing_3_fy_campaign_responses|trailing_3_fy_response_rate)", candidates)]
stopifnot(length(solicitation) > 0, !"major_donor_next_fy" %in% candidates,
          !any(grepl("^next_fy_", candidates)))
feature_sets <- list(without_solicitation = setdiff(candidates, solicitation),
                     with_solicitation = candidates)
tibble(feature = solicitation)
```

## Rolling validation and imbalance

The four algorithms use fixed, modest configurations to avoid expensive tuning
on rare positives. Each fold downsamples training negatives to at most five per
positive, keeping all positives; validation retains its natural prevalence. A
prior-odds correction maps scores back to the training population prevalence.
This correction assumes sampling depends only on the outcome; calibration must
still be checked. Imputation and zero-variance filtering are fitted separately
inside each training fold. The same sampled records are used in both feature
sets. Results are development estimates, not final-test performance.

```{r helpers}
folds <- list(`2022` = 2021L, `2023` = 2021:2022, `2024` = 2021:2023)
models <- c("Logistic regression", "Elastic Net", "Random Forest", "XGBoost")

fit_fold <- function(train, valid, features, model_name, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  y <- train$major_donor_next_fy
  if (length(unique(y)) != 2 || length(unique(valid$major_donor_next_fy)) != 2)
    stop("Each fold must contain both outcome classes")
  # Training-only preprocessing, before negative sampling.
  x <- as.data.frame(train[, features, drop = FALSE])
  v <- as.data.frame(valid[, features, drop = FALSE])
  medians <- vapply(x, function(z) if (all(is.na(z))) 0 else median(z, na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1))
  for (j in seq_along(x)) {
    x[[j]][is.na(x[[j]])] <- medians[j]
    v[[j]][is.na(v[[j]])] <- medians[j]
  }
  keep <- vapply(x, function(z) length(unique(z)) > 1, logical(1))
  x <- x[, keep, drop = FALSE]; v <- v[, keep, drop = FALSE]
  pos <- which(y == 1); neg <- which(y == 0)
  selected <- c(pos, sample(neg, min(length(neg), 5L * length(pos))))
  x <- x[selected, , drop = FALSE]
  sampled_y <- factor(ifelse(y[selected] == 1, "yes", "no"), levels = c("yes", "no"))
  population_prior <- mean(y == 1); sample_prior <- mean(y[selected] == 1)
  control <- trainControl(method = "none", classProbs = TRUE, allowParallel = FALSE)
  if (model_name == "Logistic regression") {
    fit <- train(x, sampled_y, method = "glm", family = binomial(), trControl = control)
  } else if (model_name == "Elastic Net") {
    fit <- train(x, sampled_y, method = "glmnet", family = "binomial",
                 preProcess = c("center", "scale"),
                 tuneGrid = data.frame(alpha = 0.5, lambda = 0.01), trControl = control)
  } else if (model_name == "Random Forest") {
    fit <- train(x, sampled_y, method = "rf", ntree = 200,
                 tuneGrid = data.frame(mtry = max(1L, floor(sqrt(ncol(x))))),
                 importance = TRUE, trControl = control)
  } else {
    fit <- xgboost::xgb.train(
      data = xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(as.matrix(x), label = as.integer(sampled_y == "yes")),
      params = list(objective = "binary:logistic", max_depth = 3, eta = 0.05,
                    colsample_bytree = 0.8, subsample = 0.8, nthread = 1),
      nrounds = 100, verbose = 0)
  }
  prob <- if (model_name == "XGBoost") predict(fit, as.matrix(v)) else
    predict(fit, newdata = v, type = "prob")$yes
  prob <- pmin(pmax(prob, 1e-8), 1 - 1e-8)
  corrected <- plogis(qlogis(prob) + qlogis(population_prior) - qlogis(sample_prior))
  importance <- tryCatch({
    if (model_name == "XGBoost") {
      z <- xgboost::xgb.importance(model = fit)
      data.frame(feature = z$Feature, importance = z$Gain)
    } else {
      z <- varImp(fit, scale = FALSE)$importance
      data.frame(feature = rownames(z), importance = rowMeans(z))
    }
  }, error = function(e) data.frame(feature = character(), importance = numeric()))
  list(predictions = data.frame(constituent_id = valid$constituent_id,
       fiscal_year = valid$fiscal_year, outcome = valid$major_donor_next_fy,
       probability = corrected), importance = importance)
}

# Average precision is the step-wise area under the precision-recall curve.
metrics <- function(d) {
  d <- d[order(-d$probability, d$constituent_id), ]
  y <- d$outcome; n <- length(y); positives <- sum(y); prevalence <- mean(y)
  precision <- cumsum(y) / seq_len(n)
  ap <- sum(precision[y == 1]) / positives
  roc <- as.numeric(pROC::auc(pROC::roc(y, d$probability, levels = c(0, 1), quiet = TRUE)))
  top <- lapply(c(.05, .10, .20), function(fraction) {
    k <- ceiling(n * fraction); p <- mean(y[seq_len(k)])
    data.frame(fraction = fraction, k = k, precision = p, lift = p / prevalence)
  })
  list(summary = data.frame(n = n, positives = positives, prevalence = prevalence,
       pr_auc = ap, roc_auc = roc, brier = mean((d$probability - y)^2),
       mean_probability = mean(d$probability)), top = bind_rows(top))
}
```

```{r run}
# Two workers limit memory when Windows serializes data to worker processes.
workers <- min(2L, max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L))
cluster <- parallel::makeCluster(workers)
parallel::clusterCall(cluster, function(paths) .libPaths(paths), .libPaths())
registerDoParallel(cluster)
jobs <- expand.grid(validation_year = as.integer(names(folds)),
                    feature_set = names(feature_sets), model = models,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
results <- tryCatch(foreach(i = seq_len(nrow(jobs)), .packages = c("caret", "dplyr"),
                   .export = c("fit_fold", "folds", "feature_sets", "dev", "jobs"),
                   .errorhandling = "stop") %dopar% {
  job <- jobs[i, ]
  fit_fold(dev[dev$fiscal_year %in% folds[[as.character(job$validation_year)]], ],
           dev[dev$fiscal_year == job$validation_year, ],
           feature_sets[[job$feature_set]], job$model, 1000L + job$validation_year)
}, finally = { parallel::stopCluster(cluster); registerDoSEQ() })
predictions <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(results), function(i)
  cbind(jobs[i, ], results[[i]]$predictions)))
importance <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(results), function(i)
  cbind(jobs[rep(i, nrow(results[[i]]$importance)), , drop = FALSE], results[[i]]$importance)))
```

## Performance comparisons

```{r evaluation}
groups <- split(predictions, interaction(predictions$model, predictions$feature_set,
                                        predictions$validation_year, drop = TRUE))
evaluated <- lapply(groups, function(d) {
  m <- metrics(d)
  keys <- d[1, c("model", "feature_set", "validation_year")]
  list(summary = cbind(keys, m$summary), top = cbind(keys, m$top))
})
fold_metrics <- bind_rows(lapply(evaluated, `[[`, "summary"))
top_metrics <- bind_rows(lapply(evaluated, `[[`, "top"))
fold_metrics %>% arrange(validation_year, model, feature_set) %>% as.data.frame()
top_metrics %>% arrange(validation_year, model, feature_set, fraction) %>% as.data.frame()
```

```{r comparison-plots}
ggplot(fold_metrics, aes(factor(validation_year), pr_auc, color = feature_set, group = feature_set)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line() + facet_wrap(~model) + labs(x = "Validation feature FY", y = "Average precision (PR AUC)", color = "Features") + theme_minimal()
ggplot(top_metrics, aes(factor(fraction), lift, fill = feature_set)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") + facet_grid(model ~ validation_year) +
  labs(x = "Top share", y = "Lift over validation prevalence", fill = "Features") + theme_minimal()
```

```{r paired-differences}
fold_metrics %>% select(model, validation_year, feature_set, pr_auc, roc_auc, brier) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = feature_set, values_from = c(pr_auc, roc_auc, brier)) %>%
  mutate(delta_pr_auc = pr_auc_with_solicitation - pr_auc_without_solicitation,
         delta_roc_auc = roc_auc_with_solicitation - roc_auc_without_solicitation,
         delta_brier = brier_with_solicitation - brier_without_solicitation) %>%
  arrange(model, validation_year) %>% as.data.frame()
```

## Calibration and feature importance

Calibration uses equal-count score bins within each model, feature set and
validation year. Brier score and mean prediction versus prevalence are reported
above. Bins can contain very few positives; calibration is descriptive and the
prior correction is not a substitute for independent calibration.

```{r calibration}
calibration <- predictions %>% group_by(model, feature_set, validation_year) %>%
  mutate(bin = ntile(probability, 10)) %>% group_by(model, feature_set, validation_year, bin) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), predicted = mean(probability), observed = mean(outcome), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(calibration, aes(predicted, observed, color = feature_set)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2) + geom_point(aes(size = n)) +
  facet_grid(model ~ validation_year, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Mean predicted probability", y = "Observed rate", color = "Features") + theme_minimal()
```

```{r importance}
# Importance scales differ between algorithms; compare within a model/fold only.
importance %>% filter(feature_set == "with_solicitation") %>%
  group_by(model, validation_year) %>% slice_max(importance, n = 12, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>% arrange(model, validation_year, desc(importance)) %>% as.data.frame()
```

## Interpretation and limitations

Focus on paired differences by year, especially precision and lift at realistic
staff capacity. Class imbalance makes ROC AUC alone misleading. Few positive
outcomes make fold metrics and importance unstable; assess uncertainty and
repeatability before operational use. Importance is model-specific, not causal,
and correlated giving and solicitation variables can share importance. The
fixed model settings are a computational baseline, not exhaustive tuning.
Random downsampling and prior correction may still produce poorly calibrated
scores; temporal drift and repeated constituents across years affect evaluation.
All data are synthetic, with release-specific cleaning and placeholder fields.
A later final-group workflow should freeze model and features, fit on development
years, and evaluate FY2025 once; FY2026 can only be scored until FY2027 labels
are available. Do not interpret these results as an estimate of the causal effect
of solicitation or of the cultivation program.
